newsitem.title: THAILAND: FOCUS-Thai currency firms after intervention.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Thai currency firms after intervention.

text.p: Thailand successfully defended its embattled currency on Thursday with central bank intervention, a squeeze on liquidity and reassurances that there were no plans to devalue.
Several Asian central banks cooperated with Thailand by jointly intervening to defend the embattled baht against speculative attacks, Thai deputy central bank governor Chaiyawat Wibulswasdi said.
The baht was quoted sharply firmer at 25.250/25.350 late on Thursday against 25.910/25.940 early in the morning and 26.330/26.430 late on Wednesday.
"The central bank would like to ask the private sector to have confidence in the government policy and not to listen to the rumours," the Bank of Thailand said earlier in a statement.
"The central bank wishes to stress that there would be no devaluation or changes in the currency exchange mechanism which were mentioned by rumours," it said.

In Singapore, dealers said the Thai central bank had ordered local banks not to quote tomorrow/next rates in the baht to offshore parties, effectively cutting off a source of short-term borrowing to fund speculation.

Thai Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan on Thursday also repeated the government's determination to guard the currency against speculative attacks. He said in Tokyo the government's defence of the baht has been, and will be, successful.

Rising concerns about the slowing Thai economy and rumours of political turmoil in the cabinet that could lead to Amnuay's possible resignation triggered heavy baht sales for the dollar on Wednesday. Amnuay has repeatedly denied he would quit.
"(On Wednesday) there was fierce speculation on the baht in the overseas market," the central bank statement said. "At present the situation has eased to a certain degree."

The central bank and the Monetary Authority of Singapore jointly intervened in the foreign exchange market on Wednesday to defend the baht. Malaysia's central bank and the Hong Kong Monetary Authority also bought the Thai currency, trade sources said, although their intervention was not confirmed.
The Bank of Japan said on Thursday that, if asked, it may intervene in the market to help support the baht under a 1996 Asian currency safety net agreement.

Last year monetary authorities of Australia, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, the Philippines, Singapore and Thailand agreed to establish bilateral repurchase agreements to provide liquidity in times of currency crisis.

Amnuay said that Thailand has support "from all our friends" in its currency defence. He also moved to soothe fears about the deterioration in the Thai economy, saying the country was "in a process of recovery."
The economy had gone through its worst, he said, adding he was pleased with a sharp decline in the current account deficit and inflation, and expectations that exports were improving.
The market rumours also hit the Thai bourse on Thursday, causing the market to drop to near eight-year lows. The main index closed at 557.87 points, a fall of 2.35 percent.
Thailand's currency woes have unnerved other markets in the region with the Philippine peso, the Malaysian ringgit and the Indonesian rupiah also suffering heavy selling.

The statement, which came after heavy speculative attacks on the baht this week and a plunge in the stock market index to near eight-year-lows, said the premier's office also provided reassurance that the Thai economic situation remained stable.
To fight baht speculators, the central bank intervened heavily in the local and foreign markets, especially on Wednesday when the run on the currency heightened.
It also sought assistance from regional counterparts to fight speculators and received support from them, a senior central bank official said.

The statemet said inflation had decreased from seven percent last year to 4.4 percent and the forecasted current account deficit was expected to be six percent of gross domestic product at the end of this year compared to over eight percent last year, it added.
The structure of the long term debt had risen to 60 percent from 50 percent, it added.

"Next week Mr. Amnuay Viravan and the Governor of the Bank of Thailand are also preparing to announce additional measures to promote confidence in the Thai economy and financial institutions as well as measures to increase its liquidity," the statement said.
"As a result there are no reasons whatsoever to devalue the baht currency," it added.
The baht rallied late on Thursday supported by regional central bank intervention and was quoted at 25.300/400 against the dollar compared with 26.330/430 late on Wednesday.
